raw_response:
I will still do mostly what has worked for me before, because 15 mu is not small and I cannot gamble on a bad harvest. With wheat-maize, I know the land, I have well water, and I have farmed 40 years, so I will keep the main area in that rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around here, if wheat fertilizer is too light, the heads stay short; if maize is short of fertilizer at jointing, yield drops fast. So I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. I will put about 10 mu into wheat-maize rotation and 5 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, rotary till after the last crop, give enough base fertilizer, then chase nitrogen once more in spring, with 3 irrigations if water is normal. For maize after wheat, I will go with hybrid seed because the better ones usually yield more if water and fertilizer keep up; I will use a little heavier nitrogen than cotton and irrigate 2 times. Cotton is slower money and takes more watching, but on part of the land it still gives me cash, so I will keep 5 mu, use improved seed, not be stingy on potash, and spray more times because insects on cotton are never light. I look at what nearby farmers do, what the seed and fertilizer dealer says, and what worked on my own field last year, then I adjust a little, not too much.
